headline: EPS beats on cost discipline; Grasberg ramp weighs on volume
summary_short: Q2 2026 EPS of $0.68 (+28% y/y) beat despite copper production down 18% at 786M lbs on the Grasberg Block Cave ramp. Realized copper $6.17/lb (+36% y/y) drove margin; unit cash costs jumped to $1.97/lb from $1.13.
summary_long: Q2 2026 net income $984M ($0.68 diluted; adjusted $0.74) on revenue $7.03B (-7% y/y). Copper sales 710M lbs beat April 690M estimate but volume down from 1.02B Q2 2025 as PTFI Grasberg Block Cave stays in phased ramp-up. Realized prices lifted margins: Cu $6.17/lb (+36% y/y), Au $4,520/oz (+37%), moly $28.75/lb (+36%). Unit net cash costs $1.97/lb favorable to $2.24 April estimate on moly credits but above $1.13 Q2 2025 on fixed-cost absorption. Operating cash flow $2.05B (net $0.6B working-capital use); capex $1.10B. FY2026 guidance: 3.1B lbs Cu, 650koz Au, 93M lbs moly sales; cash cost $1.90/lb; capex $4.3B. Net debt $2.1B; repurchased 1.7M shares for $110M; Cerro Verde ownership to 55.66%.
confidence_notes: Unit net cash costs and adjusted EPS exclude PTFI idle-facility/restoration charges ($284M in Q2, $690M YTD) tied to the September 2025 external mud rush incident — these are recurring for now until Grasberg returns to normal capacity. Copper cash cost jump ($1.13→$1.97) is volume-driven fixed-cost absorption, not input inflation.
